baseline.heading: Review boundaries
baseline.description: One research README section only: exploratory trial, no controlled benchmark, no measured token savings, no automatic publishing

retrieval_candidates.why: Both sections bound what the retrieval experiment establishes; research README summarizes limitations expressed in the paper
The README's exploratory-trial characterization concerns the paper experiment protocol
The README explicitly rejects a token-savings claim; the paper identifies economics evaluation as separate
Coverage records which capabilities have executable evidence versus open measurement limitations
Replay report supplies source and retrieval verification; it does not turn the experiment into a benchmark
GPS documentation records an original navigation result and explicitly calls it non-benchmark
Paper's artifact and authorship note addresses publication and source provenance

evidence_limitations: No measured accuracy or token benefit
Cross-file qualified semantic edges are proposed, not human-reviewed

before.question: What does the review boundaries section prove and not prove?
before.finding: The research was one exploratory trial, not a controlled benchmark. The section disclaims measured token savings, restricts prior-work coverage, and states that no automatic submission/publishing occurred.

after.question: What does the review boundaries section prove and not prove?
new_supported_details: The paper distinguishes selective retrieval mechanics from measured token efficiency or general retrieval accuracy.
The manuscript describes its protocol and separately enumerates what the result does not prove.
The GPS experiment documentation records the selected source passages and describes it as a recorded result, not an automated benchmark.
The evidence-and-replay document documents historical identifiers and a reconstruction, which should not be confused with an independently controlled model evaluation.
The coverage matrix separately distinguishes implemented library features and unmeasured semantic retrieval quality.
Authorship/provenance and economics-evaluation sections add boundaries beyond the original README paragraph.
not_established: General effectiveness across independent agents or sessions
Human-reviewed validation of the proposed cross-document semantic edges

comparison.assessment: Richer source-grounded coverage of limitations and provenance; no change to the underlying observed experiment
comparison.caution: This is a qualitative same-question comparison, not a controlled retrieval-quality measurement
